The mood of each citizen is base-city-happiness's calculator, and lib/calculateCitizenState re-exports it. Civil disorder and celebration are kept with base-city-happiness-status, under the same save ids and events. Martial law is base-government-martial-law's, with Civ1's governments, limit of 3 and one citizen per unit as its table. Military unhappiness is base-government-military-unhappiness's, with Civ1's 1 under a Republic and 2 under a Democracy. Rule ids, priorities, numbers and exports are unchanged, so Civ1 plays the same.

Civ1's cap (an Aqueduct at 10), its pollution numbers, polluting advances, Mass Transit and the roll's 256 stay here; the mechanisms are base-city-growth-limit's and base-city-pollution's, so Civilization II can share them. Rules/PollutionDivisor re-exports base-city-pollution's class, so the rules registered from that path still apply, and lib/pollute and lib/pollution keep their signatures. Nothing changes in play (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008).

The power ranking's terms and units' strength are computed by @civ-clone/base-power; the rule ids, the weights (gold/32, 8 per citizen, advances, unit cost/10), the Nuclear exclusion and the rule order stay here. No change in play (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008).

Civ1's prices (r²/20 + 2r for a unit, 2r for an improvement, 4r for a Wonder or spaceship part, doubled with nothing stored), the civil-disorder criterion and the save's civ1-treasury:sold record stay here; the formulas and the record's keeping are base-treasury's, so Civilization II can share them. Nothing changes in play (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008).
